screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled pilot RCT evaluating intracervical nitroprusside gel vs placebo for reducing IUD insertion-related pain. Primary outcome was subject-reported pain with IUD insertion, with additional pain measurements at other time points including immediately after insertion.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating ibuprofen 800mg vs placebo for pain reduction during IUD insertion. Measured pain immediately following IUD insertion using VAS. Meets criteria as RCT with intervention for preventing insertion-related pain.

Randomised trial comparing delayed vs immediate bladder emptying (full bladder vs empty bladder) as an intervention for IUD insertion. Outcomes included women's pain scores. This non-pharmacological intervention RCT evaluates pain during the procedure.

Randomized, open, parallel-group clinical trial comparing intracervical lidocaine injection vs oral ibuprofen in women without previous vaginal delivery. Evaluated pain immediately after, 2 hours after, and 6 hours after LNG-IUS insertion using multiple pain scales. Meets criteria for pain outcomes up to six hours post-insertion.

Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT evaluating 800 mg ibuprofen vs placebo 45 minutes prior to LNG-IUS insertion. Measured pain with tenaculum placement and during insertion. Directly addresses prevention of insertion-related pain.

Double-blinded, multicenter RCT comparing vaginal misoprostol 400μg vs placebo administered 3 hours prior to IUD insertion. Secondary outcome was pain during insertion. Evaluates pharmacological intervention for preventing insertion-related pain.

Randomized, double-blinded trial of buccal misoprostol 400mcg vs placebo 90 minutes prior to IUD insertion. Measured patient-reported pain at multiple time points: tenaculum placement, IUD insertion, and 5 minutes post-insertion. Evaluates intervention for preventing pain at all relevant time points.

Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT evaluating sublingual misoprostol 400mcg vs placebo for repeat LNG-IUS insertion. Measured pain at insertion. Addresses intervention for preventing insertion-related pain in a specific population (repeat insertion).

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of large sample size (n=2019) evaluating prophylactic ibuprofen 400mg vs placebo. Measured pain immediately after insertion using VAS. Directly evaluates prevention of insertion pain.

Single-blind randomized controlled trial comparing sublingual misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone in women with no previous vaginal delivery. Measured pain during IUD insertion. Evaluates cervical ripening agent as intervention for preventing insertion pain.

Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study (actually describes two separate RCTs) evaluating ibuprofen 600mg vs placebo before and after IUD insertion. Pain was assessed during insertion, 4-6 hours after, and for three days. Meets criteria with primary outcomes at insertion and up to six hours post-insertion.

Randomized, double-blinded clinical trial comparing oral tramadol 50mg, naproxen sodium 550mg, and placebo 1 hour before IUD insertion. Pain intensity was evaluated using VAS immediately after insertion. Three-arm RCT evaluating pharmacological interventions for preventing insertion pain.

Double-blinded, randomized, controlled trial of self-administered buccal misoprostol 400mcg vs placebo in nulliparous women. Measured pain immediately prior to, and after IUD insertion. Evaluates self-administered intervention for preventing insertion-related pain.

Randomized, double-blinded clinical trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo applied prior to uterine sounding. Measured pain at multiple time points including uterine sounding and IUD insertion. Evaluates local anesthetic intervention for preventing pain during the procedure.

Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled pilot study of vaginal nitroglycerin gel 0.5mg vs placebo 30 minutes prior to IUD placement. Primary outcome was subject-reported pain with IUD deployment. Meets criteria as RCT evaluating pharmacological intervention for preventing insertion pain.

Randomized trial comparing 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no local anesthetic. Measured pain on VAS at various points: speculum insertion, tenaculum placement, paracervical block administration, IUD insertion, and 5 minutes post-procedure. Evaluates local anesthetic intervention for preventing pain at all relevant time points.

Randomized double-blind controlled trial with three groups: lidocaine 2% gel, lubricant gel, and no intervention. Measured pain during IUD insertion using VAS. Evaluates topical anesthetic intervention for preventing insertion pain.

Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled pilot study of intrauterine lidocaine infusion vs normal saline. Measured pain at tenaculum placement and during IUD insertion. Evaluates novel local anesthetic delivery method for preventing insertion-related pain.

Randomized controlled trial of sublingual misoprostol 400μg + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone in nulliparous women. Measured pain during IUD insertion. Evaluates cervical priming as intervention for preventing insertion-related pain.

Double-blind randomized clinical trial of vaginal misoprostol 400μg vs placebo 4 hours prior to IUD insertion in nulligravidas. Measured pain during insertion as secondary outcome (significant reduction in moderate-to-severe pain shown). Evaluates intervention for preventing insertion-related pain.

Randomized controlled trial of inhaled lavender vs placebo inhaled 30 minutes before IUD insertion. Measured pain using VAS immediately after insertion. Non-pharmacological intervention (aromatherapy) evaluated for preventing insertion-related pain and anxiety.

Randomized controlled trial of self-administered vaginal or buccal misoprostol 400μg vs placebo 3-4 hours before IUD insertion. Measured pain before insertion, immediately post-insertion, and before clinic discharge. Evaluates self-administered intervention for preventing insertion-related pain at multiple time points.

Randomized controlled trial (phase II) of novel topical lidocaine formulation vs placebo for IUD insertion. Measured pain during first 10 minutes after insertion and at 30 minutes post-insertion. Evaluates novel topical anesthetic formulation for preventing/reducing insertion-related pain.

Prospective, controlled study with three arms: paracervical block with 1% lidocaine, placebo, and no treatment. Measured pain during tenaculum placement, IUD insertion, and 5 minutes after. Despite being described as 'prospective, single-blinded', the three-group design suggests randomization. Evaluates local anesthetic intervention for preventing pain at all relevant time points.

Registered clinical trial (RCT) of misoprostol 400μg vs placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women. Measured pain immediately after insertion. Evaluates misoprostol for preventing insertion-related pain in nulliparous population.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of self-administered 2% vaginal lidocaine gel vs placebo 5 minutes before IUD insertion. Measured pain during insertion. Evaluates self-administered topical anesthetic for preventing insertion pain, with tenaculum placement pain as secondary outcome.

Randomized clinical trial with three groups: lavender, sesame oil (placebo), and control. Measured pain after IUD insertion. Non-pharmacological aromatherapy intervention administered before insertion to prevent pain. Despite pain being measured after insertion, the timing falls within the 'up to six hours' window.

Descriptive article discussing a method/technique for local anesthesia during IUD insertion. Not a randomized controlled trial - describes the author's experience and technique without control groups or randomization.
Prospective cohort study, not a randomized controlled trial. Compares pain between groups with different delivery histories but does not evaluate an intervention.
Qualitative study exploring perceptions and reasons for non-use of IUDs. Not a randomized controlled trial and does not evaluate any pain prevention intervention.
Review article providing consensus recommendations and practical advice. Not original research and not a randomized controlled trial.
Methodological article about GRADE guidelines for rating evidence quality. Not a clinical trial and unrelated to the specific review question.
Clinical practice guideline/committee opinion. Not original research or a randomized controlled trial evaluating pain interventions.
Review article critically evaluating evidence for pain management strategies. Not a randomized controlled trial itself.
Review article about misoprostol use in gynecology. Not an original randomized controlled trial.
Observational study evaluating pain response without testing any intervention. Does not meet RCT requirement and is not testing pain prevention strategies.
Methodological article about GRADE system. Not a clinical trial evaluating interventions.
Non-randomized study (level of evidence II) identifying predictors of painful insertion. Does not evaluate any intervention for pain prevention.
Review article discussing pain management strategies. Not an original randomized controlled trial.
Systematic review of intrauterine anesthesia for various gynecologic procedures. Not an original RCT evaluating IUD insertion pain prevention specifically.
Observational cohort study exploring use of analgesia before IUD fitting. Not a randomized controlled trial, as women chose themselves whether to take analgesia.
Clinical practice guideline/technical report. Not a randomized controlled trial evaluating pain interventions.
Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Not an original RCT itself, but rather a synthesis of existing trials.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating nitric oxide donors for cervical ripening before surgical termination of pregnancy (abortion), not for IUD insertion. Outcome is cervical ripening, not IUD insertion pain prevention.
Survey study of doctors' practices and opinions. Not a randomized controlled trial evaluating interventions.
Methodological paper describing the approach to developing a prospective meta-analysis. Not a clinical trial evaluating pain prevention interventions.
Commentary/narrative review article discussing existing evidence. Not an original randomized controlled trial.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating treatment of pain AFTER IUD insertion, not prevention. The review specifically includes RCTs evaluating interventions for PREVENTING insertion-related pain, not treating it afterwards.
Descriptive article describing a technique for paracervical block. Not a randomized controlled trial with control groups.

Cochrane review summarizing randomized controlled trials. Not an original RCT itself. Also focuses on treatment of pain associated with IUD use (post-insertion), not prevention of insertion-related pain.
